items.q: Look! The lion dance team ______ down our street right now.
items.vi: Nhìn kìa! Đội múa lân đang đi xuống phố nhà mình ngay lúc này.
items.explanation: Look! and right now mark an action in progress at the moment of speaking, so the present continuous is coming is needed. ✗ comes — present simple is for habits and facts, not what is happening now; ✗ has come — present perfect says the arrival is already finished, which clashes with right now; ✗ came — past simple puts the action in the past, not now.

items.q: In the south of Viet Nam, the rainy ______ usually lasts from May to November.
items.vi: Ở miền Nam Việt Nam, mùa mưa thường kéo dài từ tháng Năm đến tháng Mười Một.
items.explanation: A season is a part of the year with its own weather — the rainy one here runs from May to November. ✗ term — a division of the school year, not of the weather; ✗ era — a long period of history; ✗ decade — a period of ten years, far longer than six months.

items.q: The forecast says a ______ wind will blow from the north tonight, so bring a jacket.
items.vi: Dự báo nói tối nay sẽ có gió mạnh thổi từ phía bắc, nên hãy mang theo áo khoác.
items.explanation: The collocation is a strong wind (or a light wind); the clue is wind will blow. ✗ heavy — goes with rain, snow and traffic, not wind; ✗ thick — describes fog, smoke or hair; ✗ large — describes size, and wind has no size.

items.q: Since Mai joined the school drama club, she has really ______ — she chats with everyone now.
items.vi: Từ khi Mai vào câu lạc bộ kịch của trường, bạn ấy thật sự đã cởi mở hơn hẳn — giờ bạn ấy trò chuyện với tất cả mọi người.
items.explanation: The clue she chats with everyone now shows Mai has stopped being shy: to come out of your shell is to become confident and sociable. ✗ come to her senses — to start thinking sensibly again; ✗ come down to earth — to become realistic after dreaming; ✗ come full circle — to return to where something started.

items.q: The tour guide ______ that the old market had been rebuilt after the fire.
items.vi: Hướng dẫn viên chỉ ra rằng khu chợ cũ đã được xây lại sau vụ cháy.
items.explanation: Pointed out that + clause: to point out is to tell people a fact they may not have noticed. ✗ pointed at — to aim your finger at a thing, so it needs a noun, not a that-clause; ✗ turned out — 'proved to be', used with it (it turned out that…), not with a person as subject; ✗ left out — to omit; the guide is giving information, not leaving it out.

items.q: The streets are completely dry this morning, so it ______ last night.
items.vi: Sáng nay đường phố khô ráo hoàn toàn, nên tối qua chắc chắn là không mưa.
items.explanation: The evidence completely dry leads to a confident conclusion that something did NOT happen in the past: can't have + past participle. ✗ must have rained — a confident conclusion that it DID rain, the opposite of the evidence; ✗ should have rained — means rain was expected or desirable, not a deduction from evidence; ✗ might rain — refers to the future, but last night is past.

items.q: There will be a fifteen-minute ______ between the two water-puppet shows, so you can buy some snacks.
items.vi: Sẽ có mười lăm phút giải lao giữa hai suất múa rối nước, nên bạn có thể mua chút đồ ăn vặt.
items.explanation: A planned break between the two shows is an interval. ✗ delay — unplanned lateness, not a scheduled pause; ✗ recess — a break at school or in court, not in a theatre programme; ✗ era — a long period of history, not fifteen minutes.

items.q: The bus ______ Nam takes to school every morning was twenty minutes late again today.
items.vi: Chiếc xe buýt mà Nam đi học mỗi sáng hôm nay lại trễ hai mươi phút.
items.explanation: The pronoun stands for a thing, the bus, and is the object of takes (Nam takes the bus), so which (or that) is used. ✗ who — only for people; ✗ whose — shows possession and must be followed by a noun (whose driver…); ✗ where — a relative adverb, so takes would be left without an object.

items.q: Very ______ pupils remembered to bring their raincoats, so most of them got soaked on the way home.
items.vi: Rất ít học sinh nhớ mang áo mưa, nên hầu hết các em bị ướt sũng trên đường về nhà.
items.explanation: Few + plural noun means 'almost no', stressing the small number — which is why most of them got soaked — and it is the only option that can follow very. ✗ a few — means 'some', a positive idea, and 'very a few' is impossible; ✗ little — for uncountable nouns, but pupils is plural countable; ✗ a little — also uncountable, and 'very a little' is impossible.

items.q: Lan ______ the lantern festival three times since she moved to Hoi An.
items.vi: Từ khi chuyển đến Hội An, Lan đã đi lễ hội đèn lồng ba lần.
items.explanation: Since she moved and three times count experience from a past point up to now, so the present perfect has visited is needed. ✗ visited — past simple needs a finished time (last year), not since; ✗ had visited — past perfect needs a later past event to be 'before', and there is none; ✗ visits — present simple describes a habit, not a total 'so far'.

items.q: On the way to the beach, Dad stopped ______ some petrol at the station near the bridge.
items.vi: Trên đường ra biển, bố dừng lại để mua xăng ở cây xăng gần cầu.
items.explanation: Stop to do = pause in order to do something else: Dad stopped the car so that he could buy petrol (on the way, at the station). ✗ buying — stop doing means to give up an activity, so he would have quit buying petrol; ✗ buy — a bare infinitive cannot follow stop; ✗ bought — two past verbs cannot stand together without and.

items.q: Please ______ your seat belt before the coach pulls out of the station.
items.vi: Vui lòng thắt dây an toàn trước khi xe khách rời bến.
items.explanation: The collocation is fasten (or do up) a seat belt, which has a buckle. ✗ tie — for shoelaces, ropes and knots, not a belt with a buckle; ✗ close — for doors, windows and lids; ✗ fix — means to repair or to attach firmly, not to buckle.

items.q: Uncle Tam is always ______: his bus leaves the depot at exactly six every morning.
items.vi: Bác Tâm lúc nào cũng đúng giờ: xe buýt của bác rời bến đúng sáu giờ mỗi sáng.
items.explanation: The clue at exactly six every morning describes someone who is always on time: punctual. ✗ temporary — lasting only a short time; ✗ recent — happening not long ago; ✗ urgent — needing action at once.

items.q: There was a thunderstorm last night; ______, the morning market opened as usual.
items.vi: Tối qua có giông bão; tuy vậy, chợ sáng vẫn mở cửa như thường lệ.
items.explanation: A storm at night, yet the market opened as usual: the second clause contrasts with the first, so the adverb of contrast nevertheless is needed. ✗ therefore — shows a result, but opening normally is not a result of a storm; ✗ moreover — adds a similar point, not an opposite one; ✗ otherwise — means 'if not', which makes no sense after a stated fact.

items.q: Somehow the whole class ______ Nam's surprise party, so it wasn't a surprise at all.
items.vi: Không hiểu sao cả lớp đã nghe phong thanh về bữa tiệc bất ngờ của Nam, nên nó chẳng còn bất ngờ chút nào.
items.explanation: The clue it wasn't a surprise at all shows the class had heard about the party in advance: to get wind of something is to hear about it, often before it is meant to be known. ✗ got the hang of — learned how to do something; ✗ got the better of — defeated or overcame; ✗ got rid of — threw away or removed.

items.q: If the weather office hadn't ruled out a storm, the boat race on the river ______.
items.vi: Nếu cơ quan khí tượng không loại trừ khả năng có bão thì cuộc đua thuyền trên sông đã bị hủy rồi.
items.explanation: The if-clause is past perfect (hadn't ruled out), so this is a third conditional about an unreal past, and the main clause takes would have + past participle: would have been cancelled. ✗ would be cancelled — second conditional, for an unreal present or future; ✗ will be cancelled — first conditional, for a real future possibility; ✗ was cancelled — a plain past fact, but the cancellation never happened.

items.q: We reached the station ten minutes ______, so we had time for a coffee before the train left.
items.vi: Chúng tôi đến ga sớm mười phút, nên có thời gian uống cà phê trước khi tàu chạy.
items.explanation: Ten minutes early = before the planned time, which is why there was time for a coffee. ✗ soon — 'in a short time from now'; 'ten minutes soon' is not English; ✗ lately — means 'recently' and cannot measure a time difference; ✗ quickly — describes speed of movement, not arriving before a time.

items.q: A number of lanterns ______ hung along the river every full-moon night in Hoi An.
items.vi: Nhiều chiếc đèn lồng được treo dọc bờ sông vào mỗi đêm rằm ở Hội An.
items.explanation: A number of + plural noun means 'many' and takes a plural verb (only the number of is singular), and every full-moon night calls for the present simple, so are hung. ✗ is — singular, breaks agreement with lanterns; ✗ has — singular, and has hung would be active, not the passive 'are hung' the sentence needs; ✗ was — singular and past, clashing with every night.

items.q: At the meeting, the head girl ______ a plan for a greener school festival.
items.vi: Tại cuộc họp, bạn nữ đại diện học sinh đã đề xuất một kế hoạch cho lễ hội trường xanh hơn.
items.explanation: Put forward a plan or idea = suggest it for discussion, which is what happens at the meeting. ✗ put off — postpone; ✗ put away — store something in its place; ✗ put up — build a tent or building, or display a poster.

items.q: ______ from the top of the hill, the whole town looks like a toy model.
items.vi: Nhìn từ đỉnh đồi, cả thị trấn trông như một mô hình đồ chơi.
items.explanation: The town does not do the seeing — it is seen — so the past participle gives a passive meaning (When it is seen from the top…). ✗ Seeing — active present participle, which would make the whole town the one who looks (a dangling participle); ✗ Having seen — active perfect participle, the same problem; ✗ To see — an infinitive of purpose ('in order to see'), not the meaning here.

items.q: By next Tet, my family ______ in this town for exactly ten years.
items.vi: Đến Tết sang năm, gia đình tôi sẽ sống ở thị trấn này tròn mười năm.
items.explanation: By next Tet (a future point) + for exactly ten years describe a period completed up to a point in the future, so the future perfect will have lived is needed. ✗ will live — future simple gives no sense of 'completed by then'; ✗ has lived — present perfect measures up to now, not up to next Tet; ✗ lived — past simple is for a finished past period.

items.q: The old tram line closed years ago; ______ most people in the city take the metro.
items.vi: Tuyến tàu điện cũ đã đóng cửa nhiều năm trước; ngày nay hầu hết người dân thành phố đi tàu điện ngầm.
items.explanation: Nowadays = at the present time, in contrast with the past (closed years ago … now the metro). ✗ lately — 'recently', and it goes with the present perfect, not present simple take; ✗ formerly — 'in the past', the opposite of the contrast needed; ✗ previously — also 'before', so it would put the metro in the past too.

items.q: ______ gets to the bus stop first should save seats for the rest of the group.
items.vi: Ai đến trạm xe buýt trước thì nên giữ chỗ cho cả nhóm.
items.explanation: Whoever = 'the person who' and is the subject of gets; the sentence is about a person who should save seats. ✗ Whatever — 'anything that', refers to things; ✗ Whichever — 'any one of a set', and on its own it needs a noun or 'of you' after it (whichever of you gets…); ✗ Whom — an object form, so it cannot be the subject of gets.

items.q: Tet ______ on a different date each year because it follows the lunar calendar.
items.vi: Tết rơi vào một ngày khác nhau mỗi năm vì nó theo lịch âm.
items.explanation: A festival or holiday falls on a date — the clue is on a different date. ✗ drops — means goes down or lets fall, not used with dates; ✗ sets — the sun sets; a date is set (fixed) by people, only in the passive; ✗ lies — a place lies somewhere (the town lies on the river), not a day.

items.q: Let's go to the flower market on Sunday morning, ______?
items.vi: Sáng Chủ nhật mình đi chợ hoa nhé?
items.explanation: The tag for Let's (a suggestion) is always shall we. ✗ will we — will you is the tag for an imperative (Open the door, will you?), and 'will we' matches nothing here; ✗ do we — tags a negative present simple statement (We don't go…, do we?); ✗ don't we — tags a positive present simple statement (We go…, don't we?), and Let's has no do to echo.
